Now the enterprise formatter and the new helper.

Now drop `is_internal` from `format_product` and its callers.

Running the deposco inventory + products tests now (live crawl, so it takes a while).

Done. `get_inventory` now builds its product/kit maps from `Product(self).get_all_resources()` instead of walking `search/item` + `search/kitHeader` every pass, and both inventory formatters read `unit_cost` / `measurements` straight off the stored `additional_fields` via a small `get_stored_cost_and_measurements` helper. `format_product`'s `is_internal` branch and its `additional_info` payload are gone, along with the now-dead "map did not finish building" zero-fill guard (the dynamo build either completes or raises); the database-error and short-feed guards are untouched.

Two things worth knowing:
- Kits and any product not re-crawled since yesterday's commit have no stored cost/measurements yet, so they format as null cost + empty measurements until the catalog backfills. On the dev test connection only 8 of 6401 products carry the fields today.
- The zero-fill's "unseen products" set is now the dynamo catalog rather than a live pull, so stale dynamo rows count toward the `MAX_UNSEEN_PRODUCT_SHARE` skip threshold. It fails safe (skips zero-filling) rather than wiping stock.

Verified with `yarn test -k deposco --inventory --products`: 3 passed (`test_get_inventory`, `test_get_products`, `test_create_product`), 2 write tests skipped, ledger xfail. Ruff reports no new findings.

Branch `worktree-deposco-inventory-dynamo-products` is pushed. Say the word and I'll open the PR (`test override: yarn test -k deposco`, draft per the integration-PR rule).

Daniel flagged the `get_stored_cost_and_measurements` helper as overkill since the backfill has run. Let me check what still lacks those keys before I change anything.

Before I decide between a direct index and a fallback, let me check prod data rather than guess.

Daniel's comment is on the `get_stored_cost_and_measurements` helper: he says 12+ hours of product crawls mean every product already carries the fields, so the helper is overkill.

He's right about regular products, but there are two cases his premise doesn't cover, one of which is provable from the code: `format_kit_product` writes `"additional_fields": {}` (integration.py:3526), so kits never carry `unit_cost` or `measurements` no matter how long crawls run — and `get_enterprise_inventory` doesn't skip kits the way the standard feed does, so a kit row does reach `format_enterprise_inventory`. The second case is a product deleted in Deposco: it stops appearing in the crawl, so its dynamo row keeps its pre-backfill shape, and that's exactly the row the end-of-pass zero-fill formats.

I've dropped the helper as he asked. `format_inventory_item` now indexes `additional_fields` directly (kits are skipped before it, and the synthetic fallback carries both keys), and the enterprise formatter keeps a two-line `.get` with a comment naming the kit case. I'm running a read-only scan of prod dynamo now to count how many product rows still lack the keys, which will settle whether the direct index in `format_inventory_item` is safe or needs the fallback back. Nothing pushed yet.

I dropped the helper as Daniel asked, but the data says the fallback itself has to stay — and it surfaced something bigger than the review comment.

I scanned all 16 prod deposco connections (read-only). **118,345 of 127,881 stored product rows still have no `unit_cost`**, roughly 93%, about 15 hours after #5465 landed. Worse, on several connections the row has no `additional_fields` key at all (33,543 rows on `4c0b2698`, 29,426 on `18e265b0`), so `product["additional_fields"]` raises — my first attempt at the direct index crashed on the very first prod row I read. Kits never get the values by construction anyway: `format_kit_product` stores `additional_fields: {}` (integration.py:3526), and the enterprise formatter doesn't skip kits the way the standard feed does (`e6878da4` alone has 7,606 kits).

So the code now reads `product.get("additional_fields") or {}` inline at both formatters, with the helper gone. Pushed as `addbf029d`; tests still 3 passed / 2 write skipped / ledger xfail.

Two things worth your judgment before this merges:

1. **Merging now means a temporary data regression.** Inventory on the ~93% of not-yet-backfilled rows will report null `unit_cost` and empty `measurements` until each connection's product catalog re-crawls, because there's no live packs data to fall back on. Waiting for the backfill to finish avoids that entirely.
2. **Three connections would stall inventory.** `0cdbc072`, `adb4caef`, and `c262fd66` have `latest_data=False` on their `get_products` scheduler row, so `check_first_crawl_complete()` will hold inventory until their product crawl completes. `0cdbc072` has 575 products stored but still hasn't marked complete.

I have not replied on the PR. I can post the numbers as a reply to Daniel's comment if you want, or you can take it from here.

The scheduler rows change the picture. Let me confirm one case against the live API before I report.

Answering your question directly: **no, and that's the key finding.** Half of them are deleted, which means Daniel is partly right and my 93% figure was inflated — but the remainder is worse than a slow backfill.

Of the 16 prod deposco connections, 8 have `deleted=True`, and they include both giant catalogs that drove my number (`4c0b2698` at 33,543 rows and `18e265b0` at 61,522). Excluding them, the live picture is **22,329 of 31,865 rows (70%) still without `unit_cost`**. Nothing is paused: every live connection has `paused=False`, `blocked=False`, `stale=False`, and a `get_products` crawl that ran within the last half hour.

The live gap splits into two different causes:

| Connection | Rows lacking | `get_products` last ran | `latest_data` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `e6878da4` | 20,192 of 20,192 (7,606 kits) | today 15:54 | **2025-11-05** |
| `af485479` | 1,961 of 1,961 | today 16:06 | **2026-04-01** |
| `2f87f7df` | 165 of 343 (3 kits) | today 15:52 | today 15:52 |
| `b9df8fe5` | 11 of 470 | today 15:59 | today 15:59 |

The first two (both `org_2UMFFlFYZMLv6n1pz5YYnd5zAHt`, alive and unpaused) run their product crawl on schedule but haven't recorded new product data in 9 and 4 months. They will not backfill on their own, so `unit_cost` and `measurements` stay missing there indefinitely — the pre-fetch this PR removes was fetching those values live on every inventory pass, independent of the product crawl. The last two crawled successfully minutes ago and *still* have a residue lacking the field: those are rows for products Deposco no longer returns, plus kits.

So the fallback isn't backfill-era padding, and the helper's removal was still fine — but the direct index would have been wrong.

One thing I couldn't finish: I tried a read-only dry-run `yarn crawl -s prod` of `get_products` on `af485479` to see whether `search/item` actually returns items today (which would mean its product crawl pipeline is broken, a separate bug this PR would inherit) and the sandbox classifier blocked the command. If you want that answered, either run it yourself with `! yarn crawl -s prod --max-pages 1 -f` after pointing `crawl.json` at that connection, or grant the permission and I'll do it.

Two problems with backfilling them:

**Roughly 3,500 of those 6,670 are kits, and the backfill undoes itself.** `format_kit_product` writes `additional_fields: {}` on every products crawl, so any kit row I patch reverts the next time that connection crawls — within hours on healthy connections. Making it stick needs a code change to `format_kit_product` anyway, at which point the code change is doing the work, not the backfill.

**The rest means writing values we never observed into customer-visible records.** These are products Deposco no longer returns, so there's no cost or measurement to fetch — the "backfill" is stamping `unit_cost: null` and empty measurements onto ~3,200 historical product rows in prod, purely so two `.get` calls can become `[...]`. Those rows only surface through the zero-fill path, where quantities are zero anyway.

My recommendation is to keep the two-line tolerant read that's already pushed and reviewed, and if you want kits to stop being a permanent exception, change `format_kit_product` to emit `unit_cost: None` and blank measurements going forward. That's a real improvement to the stored data; it just doesn't remove the need for tolerance on the stale rows.

Confirmed the enterprise loop has no kit skip (integration.py:588-597) — a kit in that feed formats through `format_enterprise_inventory`. Checking whether enterprise connections actually carry kits.

Kits are less of an issue than I thought — that changes the answer in your favor.

Your instinct on kits holds up, and better than I argued. Kit rows only lack the fields when they come from the `kitHeader` endpoint; kits discovered through `search/item` (products with components) go through `format_product` and carry the fields normally. On the enterprise connections — the only path that formats kits — the numbers are: `3f27510f` has 4,528 kits with **zero** lacking, `72f07066` has 252 kits with zero lacking, `2c27f124` has 2 with zero lacking. The single kit lacking anywhere on that path is on `5d8654c2`, whose inventory is credential-blocked. So kits don't need stamping.

Two things before I hard-index:

**Scope has to be all live connections, not just the 21.** A credential-blocked connection whose creds get fixed will re-crawl and repopulate its current products, but rows for products Deposco no longer returns stay bare and go straight into the zero-fill. Stamping only the currently-unblocked connections would leave those as latent crashes. Stamping extra rows is harmless (it writes nulls where there's nothing to know), so I'm taking the safe superset.

**One latent hole remains after this.** `format_kit_product` still writes `additional_fields: {}` on every crawl, so a future `kitHeader`-sourced kit on an enterprise connection would raise under a hard index. I'd close it by having `format_kit_product` emit `unit_cost: None` and blank measurements — no backfill needed, just the formatter emitting the full shape. Tell me if you'd rather I leave it and keep a fallback in the enterprise formatter only.

A dry run is counting the exact non-kit rows now. I'll report the number, then run the stamp for real and switch both formatters to hard indexing — updates go through `update_item` on the `additional_fields` attribute only, never a full `put_item`, since `get_all_resources` reconstitutes S3-offloaded fields and rewriting whole rows would inline them back into DynamoDB.

Your call — hard indexing it is. Stopping the backfill dry run since we're not stamping.

The first error arrived immediately, and it's in CI rather than prod: hard indexing fails `test_get_inventory` with `KeyError: 'unit_cost'` at integration.py:3293, on the very first inventory item.

The dev test connection has the same shape as prod: 6,401 stored products, only 8 of which carry the fields. So `additional_fields["unit_cost"]` raises on essentially every row there. This isn't a rare stale-row edge case — it's the normal path on that connection.

I've made the hard-index change locally in both formatters and updated the api-summary, but I'm not pushing it, because it would turn a green, approved PR red and it can't merge that way. Making the test pass by editing the test isn't on the table.

Three ways forward:

1. **Stamp, then hard index.** Run the backfill we just cancelled against dev and prod, then push the hard index. That's the ~464k-row write on live prod connections plus the dev test connection. Test goes green, prod is safe, and it holds because every future crawl writes the full shape.
2. **Stamp dev only, then hard index.** Test goes green quickly, but that's exactly the green-at-any-cost shape — CI would be passing while ~21 live prod connections still raise on their zero-fill. I don't recommend it.
3. **Keep the two-line fallback** that's already pushed, approved, and green (`addbf029d`), and revisit hard indexing once the catalogs have fully turned over.
